ledger.claim: The deviation the rider complains of is established by the platform's own record, not merely asserted: EV-TRIP-06015 logs a route_deviation_detected event at 14:04:24 (the vehicle left the recommended route at the TPE / Tampines Avenue 1 exit, the recommended route being the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway) and a route_rejoined event at 14:13:34, and the recorded actual route ran via Tampines Avenue 1 and Bedok North Avenue 1. The GPS trace in EV-GPS-06015 reports the same road sequence fix by fix. The rider's account that the driver left the KPE for Tampines and Bedok North is therefore corroborated on this trip's own evidence.

The driver gave the rider no notice of the deviation before or at the point of it. EV-CHAT-06015 is a contiguous chat log with 0 messages and no first or last message timestamp, and EV-TRIP-06015 records chat_message_count 0 together with an empty in_app_calls array. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation; with no chat message and no call recording in the record, the reroute is not an agreed one and the notification limb of POL-RD-21 is not met.

The reroute was not traffic-justified on the data the policy recognises. EV-ADVIS-06015-01, the LTA record for the recommended KPE segment overlapping the trip window, returns type NONE - 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window', speed bands 5-6 - and its derived block sets justifies_reroute false on the ground that type NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident). The driver's explanation that the 'KPE exit slip road got queue' is a bare assertion in the counterparty statement, and POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute.

The rider does not stretch the record, and puts the deviation to the judge on the numbers the policy directs. On the platform's recorded distances in EV-TRIP-06015 the deviation is 0.90 km (11.9 minus 11.0), which is within the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so the rider does not press the '3 km' estimate or the 4.00 SGD headline, and the rider accepts that a within-tolerance deviation engages the no-refund rows of POL-RD-24. What the rider asks the judge to weigh is that this was a non-traffic-justified deviation, for which POL-RD-24's measure is the excess distance fare - 0.90 km times the recorded 0.72 SGD/km rate in EV-FARE-06015, i.e. 0.65 SGD, not the trip fare - and that the driver's departure from the KPE was neither justified under POL-RD-23 nor notified under POL-RD-21.

The deviation distance is fixed by the platform's own recorded distances under POL-RD-22: actual route distance 11.9 km minus recommended route distance 11.0 km = 0.90 km. That is at or below the 1.0 km tolerance the same clause sets, so this trip's route change is within tolerance and nothing is payable for it.

The rider's account of a '3 km detour' is not supported by the record. The platform telemetry records a 0.90 km deviation, and POL-RD-22 requires the deviation to be measured from the recorded distances, not from the GPS trace or from the rider's recollection of the map. The rider's figure is contradicted by the evidence it would have to displace.

Under POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and both tolerance rows refuse the rider money: row (e) (not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less) and row (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation 1 km or less) each prescribe NO_ACTION. The LTA advisory for the recommended KPE segment is type NONE - no closure, congestion or incident - so POL-RD-23 does not make the reroute traffic-justified; but that only selects row (e), which still returns no refund.

The contact obligation in POL-RD-21 does not change the arithmetic. The chat log carries zero messages and the trip record lists no in-app calls, so no notice of the reroute is evidenced; but whether or not the rider was informed, POL-RD-24's outcome is invariant here, because the deviation did not exceed the 1 km tolerance and both tolerance rows (c) and (e) return NO_ACTION. The failure to notify is not a ground for money where the deviation itself is within tolerance.

NO_ACTION is party-relative, and on this record it is a driver's outcome. The rider filed the dispute and the fare stands at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION preserves the present payment state: the rider's claim for a 4.00 SGD refund fails and the metered fare of 15.87 SGD remains with the driver. POL-GEN-03 is explicit that NO_ACTION never restores or creates a charge - it simply leaves the charge standing - and no driver compensation is claimed or owed on this trip.

No open question remains, so escalation under POL-GEN-26 or POL-RD-25 would be unnecessary and would hold the fare against the driver. The contested value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so an AI ruling is final at any confidence; POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied because ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false; and the deviation and its tolerance are settled on the recorded distances, which are complete and carry full admissibility weight (1.0). The case should be decided, not referred.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the claim for a refund fails on the record, and nothing is owed either way.

What happened on the trip is not in doubt. EV-TRIP-06015 logs the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the TPE / Tampines Avenue 1 exit at 14:04:24 and rejoining at Kaki Bukit Avenue 1 / Bedok North Avenue 1 at 14:13:34, and the fix-by-fix GPS trace in EV-GPS-06015 shows the same road sequence (Tampines Avenue 1, then Bedok North Avenue 1). So the rider is right that the driver left the KPE, and the driver's assertion of a queue at the KPE exit slip road is not supported by any recognised traffic data.

What decides the money, though, is the size of the deviation, and POL-RD-22 fixes it at the platform's own recorded distances: EV-TRIP-06015 gives an actual route distance of 11.9 km against a recommended route distance of 11.0 km, a deviation of 0.90 km. That is at or below the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. The rider's "3 km detour" and the 4.00 SGD headline are therefore not supported; the recorded figure is 0.90 km.

The LTA record for the recommended KPE segment (EV-ADVIS-06015-01, type NONE, speed bands 5-6) shows no closure, congestion or incident, so POL-RD-23 does not make the reroute traffic-justified. On POL-RD-24's matrix, exactly one row applies, and this is row (e): not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less. Row (e) prescribes no refund. Row (c) would give the same result even if the reroute were justified, because a deviation within the 1 km tolerance returns no refund either way. The excess-distance measure the rider points to (0.90 km x the recorded 0.72 SGD/km rate = 0.65 SGD) belongs only to deviations over 1 km, under rows (b) and (d); it does not apply here.

The missed notification under POL-RD-21 is also established: EV-CHAT-06015 carries 0 messages and EV-TRIP-06015 records chat_message_count 0 with an empty in-app calls array, so no notice of the reroute is evidenced. But that does not change the arithmetic, because POL-RD-24's tolerance rows return NO_ACTION whether or not the rider was informed. The driver's separate points are accepted as well: the metered fare of 15.87 SGD stands (EV-FARE-06015, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and no driver compensation is claimed or owed.

On who decides: the contested value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so an AI ruling is final at any confidence; POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied because ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false; and both carriers of the deciding fact (EV-TRIP-06015 and EV-ADVIS-06015-01) carry full admissibility weight of 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the ruling clears POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar.

Result: NO_ACTION, party-relative to the rider who filed. The rider is owed nothing, no amount is refunded or charged, and the present state stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
